tier_reason: README Benchmarks table (1M iterations) compares ArenaPro against the author's own stdArena (naive new[] + linear-scan) baseline; benchmark code and a Google Benchmark JSON (benchmarks/baselines/v1.0.0/v1.0.0.json) are public, but the run was on a GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner (4 CPUs @ 4342 MHz, no CPU model) with clang Release and no explicit flags, and the baseline is not a recognized incumbent, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table at 1M iterations: Reset + refill 101.67 ms vs 14.16 s (+13825.6%); failure path 308.34 us vs 1.76 s; Allocate<T>() large 821.41 us vs 1.63 ms (+98.2%); Allocate() large 680.08 us vs 1.27 ms (+86.9%); over-aligned 770.38 us vs 1.27 ms (+64.8%); small 1.11 ms vs 1.30 ms (+17.2%). Slower on Destroy<T>() trivial (-3.7%), Allocate() 4 KiB buffer (-23.3%) and Construction (40.12 ms vs 7.47 ms, -81.4%).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang (ubuntu-latest apt package), CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release via .github/workflows/benchmark.yml; no explicit optimization flags stated
corrections.hardware: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner (context block: 4 CPUs, 4342 MHz, 48 KiB L1d, 1 MiB L2, 32 MiB L3; CPU model not recorded), Google Benchmark v1.9.1
corrections.caveats: Baseline is the author's own naive stdArena (new[] + linear scan), not malloc or a known arena library; the largest ratios compare an O(1) reset/bounds-check with a baseline that grows or frees per object. Arena is slower on Construction, Destroy and the 4 KiB buffer case. Numbers from a shared CI runner with no CPU model. Baseline JSON lives at benchmarks/baselines/v1.0.0/v1.0.0.json (not benchmarks/baselines/v1.0.0.json as the README says).

notes: Real, well-tooled header-only arena, but the comparison is against a strawman baseline; keep at C with the baseline caveat. Last commit 2026-10-04 and 1 star confirmed on github.com.

tier_reason: README table (i5-12450H, Windows 11, MSVC 2022 x64-Release) matches the claimed numbers and benchmarks/bench_allocator.cpp is public, but no compiler flags are stated (CMakeLists sets none; x64-Release is a Visual Studio configuration name, no CMakePresets.json in the repo), so not A; first-party, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table: Single int allocate+free 2,731 ns vs 29,067 ns (10.6x); std::string create+destroy 7,240 vs 19,826 ns (2.7x); bulk 10,000 allocations 54,860 vs 433,902 ns (7.9x); throughput 188M vs 23M ops/s (8.1x). Per bench_allocator.cpp each 'single' iteration is a loop of 1024 alloc+free pairs (about 2.7 ns vs 28 ns per pair, derived from page data) and each string iteration is 256 create+destroy pairs.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC 2022, Visual Studio x64-Release configuration (optimization flags not stated)
corrections.workload: Google Benchmark: 1024 back-to-back int alloc+free pairs per iteration (pool vs malloc/free and new/delete), 256 std::string create+destroy pairs, and bulk 100/1,000/10,000 int allocations (pool releases with an O(1) reset, malloc side frees each pointer).
corrections.caveats: Bench is not like for like: the pool single-int loop reuses the same LIFO slot, and the pool bulk benchmark releases with an O(1) reset() and never uses DoNotOptimize on the returned pointers, while the malloc side frees every pointer individually. Windows UCRT malloc baseline is slow relative to glibc/mimalloc. Numbers taken from the README, not rerun. Fixed-size, single-threaded pool; thread-safety not stated. 3 commits.

notes: README speedups confirmed; harness biases recorded in caveats. MIT, 0 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-09-29.

tier_reason: README sample output compares Pool and FreeList against malloc/free with benchmark code in src/main.cpp and clang++ -O2 flags, but no CPU model is given ("Apple Silicon / Intel timings will differ"), so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README sample output, 16 B x 200000: bulk 5.68 ms malloc/free vs 0.89 ms Pool (about 6.4x, derived from page data) vs 8.06 ms FreeList (slower); churn 0.00 ms malloc vs 0.44 ms Pool vs 1.74 ms FreeList. README text: Pool 'often 5-15x faster than malloc'.
corrections.caveats: Only the Pool bulk row shows a win. The churn column shows malloc at 0.00 ms, most likely because clang elides the unused malloc/free pair in BenchMalloc's churn loop, so churn ratios are meaningless, and the README's claim that FreeList is 'clearly faster on churn' contradicts its own sample (1.74 ms vs 0.00 ms). The sample prints 2 decimals while main.cpp uses setprecision(3), so it may not be verbatim output. macOS malloc baseline, CPU unspecified; single initial commit; not thread-safe; educational project per the author.

notes: Kept at C; Pool bulk win is the only supported claim, FreeList is not shown faster. MIT, 1 star, last commit 2026-09-23 confirmed.
